recentItems.title: What if you said yes? | Nduati (Robert) Karanja | TEDxArada Live
recentItems.description:
What if one simple decision could open the door to possibilities you never imagined?

In this talk, Nduati (Robert) Karanja explores the power of saying yes to opportunities, embracing uncertainty, and stepping beyond the boundaries of what feels familiar. Through his perspective and experiences, he invites us to reconsider how a single choice can shape our journeys, transform our outlook, and create room for unexpected possibilities.

Sometimes, the turning point begins with two simple words: Yes, I will. Robert) Karanja is a financial educator, advisor, entrepreneur, and public speaker with more than 14 years of experience in the financial sector. He is the founder of Cents Sensei and Affluent Financial Consultants, where he promotes financial literacy, investment education, and informed financial decision-making through speaking, training, and digital storytelling. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Bread Was Never About Bread | Chenrui Zhang | TEDxJLHS Youth
recentItems.description: Based on the campus bakery phenomenon, this speech interprets human behavioural patterns from the perspective of behavioural economics and the concept of choice architecture. It illustrates how environment, conformity and repetition shape seemingly personal preferences. It encourages reflective pause before automatic responses so as to restore individual agency in decision making. Chenrui Zhang is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School who became fascinated with a simple question: why does everyone line up for the same campus bakery? Her curiosity led her into the world of behavioural economics and choice architecture, where she found that environment, conformity, and repetition quietly shape what we call "personal preference." In her talk, she encourages everyone to pause before their next automatic choice — and take back their agency. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Make Us the Owner of Gender Norms | Yifan Cao | TEDxJLHS Youth
recentItems.description: Centered on gender related stereotypes, this speech traces the historical origin of gender norms and cites relevant research evidence. It advocates treating gender norms as reflective reference frameworks rather than behavioural constraints. It puts forward proposals for individuals, education sectors and media to foster an inclusive society free from rigid gender prejudice. Yifan Cao is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School with a keen eye for the invisible rules that shape how people are "supposed" to behave. Curious about where gender norms come from, she traced their history and dug into the research — and came to believe these norms should be mirrors for reflection, not cages for behaviour. In her talk, she calls on individuals, educators, and the media to help build a world free of rigid prejudice. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The future belongs to the most human | Tim David | TEDxWatkins Glen
recentItems.description: As technology becomes better at performing technical tasks, human skills are becoming more valuable, not less. AI isn't replacing humanity. It's revealing which human abilities matter most. Tim David was once an international award-winning mentalist. He's since written several books on advanced communication strategies, including the Blinkist Top 10 Psychology Book of the Year, "Magic Words." He's traveled to 48 states and multiple countries around the world as a keynote speaker sharing his inspiring message about the magic of human connection at work and in life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Sobrevivi ao Feminicídio da Minha Mãe  | Ianca Alves | TEDxSete Lagoas
recentItems.description: A advogada Ianca Larissa Alves Rosa aborda em sua palestra o enfrentamento à violência doméstica e ao feminicídio a partir de sua história pessoal de superação após o assassinato de sua mãe. No contexto atual, marcado por alarmantes índices de crimes contra a mulher e pela perpetuação do controle coercitivo e do silêncio social, o relato denuncia a urgência do acolhimento e da denúncia precoce. Dessa forma, o tema redefine o conceito de legado: em vez de transmitir um pacto de omissão, medo e dor para as próximas gerações, convoca a sociedade a construir uma herança coletiva fundamentada na coragem, na proteção ativa e na garantia de que nenhuma mulher precise arriscar a vida para conquistar sua liberdade. Ianca Alves é advogada criminalista com atuação em violência doméstica e crimes sexuais, dedicada à defesa dos direitos fundamentais. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Is Traveling the Best Way to Broaden Our Horizons? | Shiman Fang | TEDxJLHS Youth
recentItems.description: This speech re-evaluates the conventional notion that travel is the primary approach to broadening horizons. It points out the limitations of knowledge acquired through travelling, and maintains that in depth daily observation paired with critical reflection yields more practical insight. It recommends active curiosity and interpersonal dialogue to gain wisdom from ordinary real life contexts. Shiman Fang is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School who loves to observe — the people around her, the small moments of daily life, the questions hidden in the ordinary. While many assume travel is the best way to broaden one's horizons, she believes that curiosity and reflection at home can take us even further. In her talk, she rethinks the meaning of "seeing the world" and invites the audience to find wisdom in everyday life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Honor the Hesitation in the Darkness | Chen Ji | TEDxJLHS Youth
recentItems.description: Taking Winston Churchill’s lifelong struggle with depression (the “black dog”) as a case, this speech addresses adolescent mental distress. It presents relevant statistical data on youth mental health, underscoring that mental disorders carry no stigma and professional support should be sought when needed. It highlights persistence and resolution as core strengths for overcoming internal adversity. Chen Ji is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School who cares deeply about mental health. Inspired by Winston Churchill's lifelong battle with his "black dog" of depression, he wants his peers to know that struggling in the dark is not a weakness — and that seeking help is a kind of strength. In his talk, he shares stories and statistics to remind everyone that persistence through hesitation can lead us out of the darkness. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How to Prove You Are a Human? | Yi Tian | TEDxJLHS Youth
recentItems.description: Against the backdrop of advancing artificial intelligence, this speech discusses human uniqueness amid the failure of traditional CAPTCHA verification. Taking Turkish abrash handicraft as an example, it identifies imperfection and emphasis on experiential process as core human attributes. It holds that real world experiences and inherent flaws constitute humanity’s distinctive marks. Tianyi is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School who keeps up with every leap in artificial intelligence — and keeps asking what makes us human in the first place. When CAPTCHAs began failing to tell people from machines, he found his answer in the imperfect patterns of Turkish abrash handicraft: our flaws, and the experiences that shape us, are exactly what no AI can copy. In his talk, he celebrates the beauty of being wonderfully, imperfectly human. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: It's Just Patrick! | Gengyuan Ye | TEDxJLHS Youth
recentItems.description: This speech investigates self-consumption triggered by unknown others’ inner mental states. Drawing on psychological theories and personal anecdotes, it demonstrates that people often assume worst-case scenarios under information deficiency. It proposes establishing interpersonal trust and conducting direct communication to mitigate irrational anxiety generated by speculative imagination. Gengyuan Ye is a Senior 2 student at Jinling High School who once spent countless nights imagining the worst about what others thought of him — and then decided to find out why. Drawing on psychological theories and his own anecdotes, he discovered how easily speculation fills the gaps when information is missing. In his talk, he shares how trust and direct communication can quiet the noise inside our heads. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Sintonizzati altrove | Francesco Sbraccia | TEDxToranoNuovo
recentItems.description:
Perché scegliamo la musica che ci accompagna ovunque? Francesco Sbraccia esplora il paesaggio sonoro dell’Homo digitalis, tra playlist personalizzate, rifugi emotivi e cuffie che diventano scudi contro il rumore del mondo. Ma quando la musica ci protegge, rischiamo anche di smettere di ascoltare ciò che ci circonda. Un viaggio tra tecnologia, identità e ascolto, alla riscoperta di una possibilità: trasformare le nostre melodie interiori da barriere a ponti, per ritrovare una sintonia con il mondo e con gli altri. FRANCESCO SBRACCIA - Compositore, pianista, cantautore e docente, affianca alla produzione musicale la ricerca sulla percezione acustica e sull’ecologia dell’ascolto.
Ha composto musiche per il teatro e per formazioni sinfoniche e cameristiche, ha insegnato all’Università di Teramo ed è stato vincitore di Musicultura. Ha inoltre curato la direzione artistica dell’album Pigri, entrato nella cinquina del Premio Tenco 2026, e si dedica alla valorizzazione della musica popolare abruzzese con il progetto Tradizioni Progressive. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The importance of art for a thriving society | Sheema Kermani | TEDxDUHS
recentItems.description:
What happens when a society loses its connection to art, culture, and empathy?

 In this powerful and thought provoking talk, legendary classical dancer and activist Sheema Kermani dissects the elements of a "dead society", one devoid of creative expression, equality, and social justice.

Drawing on decades of experience at the intersection of performing arts and human rights, she reveals how dance and theatre serve as vital lifeblood to awaken marginalized communities, challenge the status quo and breathe life back into a fractured world. This talk explores the critical space between silence and expression, proving that art is not just entertainment, but a necessary tool for survival and societal transformation.

This talk was given at TEDxDUHS, an independently organized TEDx event exploring the theme "The In Between". Sheema Kermani is a legendary Pakistani classical dancer, choreographer, and a prominent women's rights activist. She is the founder of Tehrik-e-Niswan (The Women's Movement), an organization that utilizes theatre and performing arts to advocate for marginalized communities, peace and gender equality. For decades, she has been a defining cultural icon in Pakistan, utilizing art as a powerful medium for societal transformation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Brushing the strokes of recovery: What my mirror taught me | Rabika Tahir | TEDxDUHS
recentItems.description:
How do you rebuild your sense of self when life strips away everything you thought you knew? 

For Rabika Tahir, a resilient blood cancer survivor, the journey back to health wasn't just about medicine, it was about facing the mirror and rediscovering her identity through the transformative power of art and self expression.

In this deeply moving talk, Rabika explores the intersection of severe personal health challenges and creative passion, revealing how the simple act of content creation became a profound tool for mental recovery and reclaiming her narrative.

This talk was given at TEDxDUHS, an independently organized TEDx event exploring the theme "The In Between".   Rabika Tahir represents the brilliance of our own DUHS student body as a Biotechnology student. She is a resilient blood cancer survivor who has navigated profound personal health challenges while maintaining her creative passions and academic trajectory, rabika is also an emerging content creator and makeup artist. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
